Sheet 01 · General arrangement · host-native software factory

GRANADAIntent → draft pull request

You type one line. The coding agent already in your CLI (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor) takes it down a fixed track of stations. At the end of the track is a merge-ready draft pull request.

Set up with your agent Install by hand

Sheet 02 · What it is

One line in. A draft pull request out.

Granada is a CLI that your coding agent drives. It does not bring its own model. The agent you already use does the thinking, and Granada keeps the work on a fixed track.

  1. You type/granada-feature add a dark mode toggle to the settings page
  2. The track runsSpec, review, plan, build in a worktree, test, review, check. You answer a few questions in chat.
  3. You getA draft pull request on granada/<change-id>--<run-id> and one decision page in plain words.

01Granada owns the track

Which station comes next, what each station must hand back, and the checks every answer has to pass. It records the run.

02Your agent does the thinking

At each agent station, the agent in Claude Code, Codex or Cursor writes the answer. An answer that fails its check goes back to the agent.

03Tool stations run on their own

Worktree, tests, ship checks, quality, mutation, drift, merge and forge. Granada runs these itself.

Small changes run lighter

When sizing estimates at most 5 files, 200 changed lines and 2 requirements, the run leaves out amigos, synthesizer, spec-revise and plan-review. You still approve the spec. If the built change is larger, the run goes back and runs every station.

When a station blocks

The agent tells you why. Fix what it names, then continue from that station:

granada run status --run-id <id>
granada run resume --run-id <id> --from <station>

Sheet 05 · You stay in charge

Every decision gets one page.

The track stops for you at a few points: clarify, sizing and the readable spec on a feature run, triage on a patch, the charter and the architecture on a bootstrap. The agent shows you the page before it asks for your answer.

After the build, change-brief writes the same kind of page for the whole change. To make the run stop there for your answer:

granada station set feature change-brief --human true

Sheet 06 · Agent setup

Let your agent set it up.

Paste one line into your agent, in the repository where you want Granada. The agent reads the steps and runs them: Node check, install, host sync, host doctor. It asks you before it commits.

Read https://daskinnyman.github.io/granada-release/setup-prompt.md and follow it.

Start your host CLI in your repository and paste the line. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor all work.

If your agent cannot fetch web pages, paste the full prompt instead:

setup-prompt.md · full text
Set up Granada in this repository.

Granada is a CLI that runs a one-line intent through a fixed track of
stations and ends with a draft pull request. You, the coding agent, do the
work at its agent stations. Granada runs the tool stations and the checks.

Do these steps in order. If a step fails, stop and tell me what failed.
Do not use sudo.

1. Run `node --version`. Granada needs Node.js 22.12 or newer, also when it
   is installed with Homebrew. If Node is older or missing, stop and tell me.

2. Run `granada --version`. If the command is not found, install Granada:
   - If `brew` is available:
       brew tap daskinnyman/granada https://github.com/daskinnyman/granada-release
       brew install granada
   - Else:
       curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daskinnyman/granada-release/main/install.sh | bash
     This puts `granada` in ~/.local/bin. If `granada` is still not found,
     add ~/.local/bin to PATH for this shell and tell me which shell file to
     change.

3. Run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` to check that this folder is a git
   repository. `granada host sync` refuses a folder that is not one.
   If it is not a repository and the folder is empty (a new project), ask
   me, then run `git init`. In any other case, stop and ask me.

4. Run `granada host sync`, then `granada host doctor`.
   Show me every warning or failure that doctor reports. If doctor says the
   host has not approved the `granada` MCP server, tell me how to approve it
   in this host.

5. Run `git status` and show me the files that sync wrote. Suggest that I
   commit them. Ask me before you commit.

6. Only if this repository has an `openspec/` folder, run:
       npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@1.13.2
   Plain markdown specs, Granada's default, need nothing installed.

7. If `gh` is not installed, tell me that the GitHub CLI is optional and
   lets Granada open GitHub draft pull requests.

8. If this repository has a package.json, tell me: the feature track runs a
   mutation station by default, and it needs `@stryker-mutator/core` as a
   devDependency, committed on the base branch. `granada run start` names
   the command to add it. Do not add it unless I ask.

9. Tell me the three commands I can use now:
       /granada-feature <what to add>
       /granada-patch <the bug to fix>
       /granada-bootstrap <the project to create>
   Tell me that I may need to restart this CLI so it loads the new skills.

Sheet 07 · Manual install

Install by hand.

RequiredNode.js 22.12+Granada is a Node CLI. You need Node also when you install with Homebrew or curl.
RequiredA git repositoryBootstrap can start from an empty folder, after git init.
RequiredOne host CLIClaude Code, Codex, Cursor
OptionalGitHub CLI (gh)For GitHub draft pull requests.

AHomebrew

brew tap daskinnyman/granada https://github.com/daskinnyman/granada-release
brew install granada

Update with brew upgrade granada (or granada update).

Bcurl

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daskinnyman/granada-release/main/install.sh | bash

Puts granada on PATH at ~/.local/bin. Add that directory to PATH if the command is not found. Pin a version with GRANADA_VERSION=<version>.

CConnect your host

granada host sync
granada host doctor

Run these in your repository. Sync writes the skills, the MCP server entry and the Stop hook. Doctor checks that the host sees them. Commit the files that sync wrote.

DRun a track

/granada-feature add a dark mode toggle to the settings page
/granada-patch the login form crashes when the email is empty
/granada-bootstrap a command-line todo list in TypeScript

Start your host CLI in the repository and type one of these.

OpenSpec: only if your repository uses it. Plain markdown specs, Granada's default, need nothing installed. A repository that writes its specs with OpenSpec needs version 1.13.0 or newer, installed globally so the host finds it: 
npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@1.13.2
Mutation in a Node project. The feature track runs a mutation station by default. It needs @stryker-mutator/core as a devDependency, committed on the base branch. granada run start names the command to add it. You can also turn mutation off with mutation: { enabled: false } in Granada's gates.yaml.

GRANADA

Named after a lunar crater city that builds machines.
